module_role: Synthesizable CAN-FD communication controller IP (Bosch M_CAN), integrable as stand-alone or part of an ASIC. Performs communication per ISO 11898-1:2015. Includes CAN Core + Tx/Rx Handlers + Generic Slave Interface (Host CPU) + Generic Master Interface (32-bit Message RAM) + Extension Interface (optional debug). Requires external CAN transceiver + external Message RAM.
layered_structure_summary: Object Layer — message acceptance filtering (M_CAN's Acceptance Filter + Standard/Extended Filter Elements), Tx + Rx mailbox management (dedicated buffers / FIFOs / Queue / Tx Event FIFO).
Transfer Layer (kernel) — Bit Stream Processor (BSP), Bit Timing Logic (BTL), Error Management Logic (EML), Acceptance Filter, all per ISO 11898-1:2015.
Physical Layer — outside M_CAN; external transceiver (typically ISO 11898-2 high-speed differential) translates between m_can_tx/m_can_rx logical levels and CANH/CANL voltages.

integration_overview.topology: Single shared CAN serial channel (multi-master, content-addressed, wired-AND).
integration_overview.drive_type: Wired-AND at the bus: dominant overrides recessive on simultaneous transmission.
integration_overview.no_chip_select: CAN is content-addressed by IDENTIFIER — no per-device chip-select. M_CAN's Acceptance Filter accepts/rejects per-IDENTIFIER locally.
integration_overview.uniform_arbitration_bit_rate: Arbitration bit rate (NBTP) is uniform within a CAN network. Data phase bit rate (DBTP) may be higher but must be ≥ arbitration rate.
integration_overview.max_baud_typical: Arbitration phase ≤ 1 Mbit/s typical; data phase typically 2 / 5 / 8 Mbit/s (up to 5 Mbit/s with 20 MHz m_can_cclk + 4 tq data bit time).

interface_categories: Generic Slave Interface — Host CPU register access (8/16/32-bit; protected-write semantics for configuration).
Generic Master Interface — 32-bit external Message RAM access (m_can_aeim_*).
CAN PHY interface — m_can_tx + m_can_rx to external transceiver.
Interrupt interface — m_can_int0 + m_can_int1 (per ILE / ILS / IE configuration).
TSU interface — m_can_tsrx + m_can_tstx + external 32-bit timestamp inputs (when CCCR.UTSU = 1).
DMU interface — m_can_dma_req / m_can_dma_ack (when debug-on-CAN is used).
Extension interface — all IR flags + selected internal status/control to module-external interrupt unit (optional).
Clock interface — m_can_hclk (Host clock domain) + m_can_cclk (high-precision CAN clock domain).
interconnect_topologies_supported: Single multi-master bus — all CAN nodes share one physical channel; arbitration by IDENTIFIER.
Multiple M_CANs sharing the same Message RAM (M_CAN has Generic Master Interface arbitration / hand-off for this).
Mixed Classical-CAN + CAN-FD nodes — when CCCR.FDOE = 1 on FD-capable nodes; Classical nodes must be silenced (e.g. Bus Monitoring) or programming protocol must avoid FD frames in their presence.
Mixed ISO + non-ISO CAN-FD nodes — CCCR.NISO selects which frame format is generated/accepted by an M_CAN; mixing ISO + non-ISO on the same bus is NOT interoperable.
default_signal_values_when_omitted: Bus idle = all nodes drive recessive (= released). M_CAN's m_can_tx is held recessive (HIGH) under CCCR.INIT = 1 (the reset state).
soc_dependent_items: External transceiver choice (ISO 11898-2 high-speed differential, ISO 11898-3 fault-tolerant, ISO 11898-6 partial networking, etc.).
Pull-up / termination resistor selection at the physical layer.
Crystal / oscillator selection for m_can_cclk (high-precision; must meet bit-time tolerance; CAN FD data rates demand low jitter).
m_can_hclk choice — may be spread-spectrum (FM-PLL) for EMC; must satisfy m_can_hclk ≥ m_can_cclk.
Message RAM size + ECC/parity choice (external ECC/parity logic feeds m_can_aeim_berr[1:0]).
Rx FIFO + Rx Buffer + Tx Buffer / FIFO / Queue + Tx Event FIFO element counts + start addresses.
Acceptance filter list programming + dedicated Rx Buffer mapping.
Bit-timing programming (NBTP / DBTP / TDCR) — typically with a CAN bit timing calculator.
Synthesis generic parameter choice: iso_only_g, connected_tsu_g, CREL synthesis-stamp values.

low_power_modes.sleep_mode: Triggered via m_can_clkstop_req or CCCR.CSR. After pending Tx complete + bus idle: CCCR.INIT set, m_can_clkstop_ack + CCCR.CSA = 1. m_can_hclk + m_can_cclk may be stopped. CPU can still access registers except CCCR.INIT (held = 1).
low_power_modes.wake_up: Restart clocks → CPU deasserts m_can_clkstop_req or clears CCCR.CSR → M_CAN clears m_can_clkstop_ack + CCCR.CSA → CPU clears CCCR.INIT → BSP synchronizes to bus (11 consecutive recessive bits).
low_power_modes.abort_path: If bus is heavily disturbed and idle is never reached, CCCR.INIT is not set automatically; software polls PSR.ACT and may write CCCR.INIT = 1 explicitly to stop CAN communication.

l9_contract_summary.host_cpu_protocol: Memory-mapped 32-bit register bus, 8/16/32-bit access. Protected-Write for configuration (CCCR.CCE + CCCR.INIT = 1). Read-on-clear semantics on selected status fields (PSR / ECR.CEL). Write-1-to-clear on IR flags.
l9_contract_summary.message_ram_protocol: 32-bit Generic Master Interface; M_CAN drives m_can_aeim_sel + address + write data, RAM responds with m_can_aeim_ready + read data + m_can_aeim_berr[1:0] (optional ECC/parity status). M_CAN does not check for erroneous Message RAM configuration — integrator responsibility.
l9_contract_summary.phy_protocol: Logical-level m_can_tx (output) + m_can_rx (input). External transceiver drives differential bus. Dominant = logical 0, recessive = logical 1.
l9_contract_summary.interrupt_protocol: Two CPU lines (int0 / int1) per ILE; per-flag enable + line-select via IE + ILS; W1C semantics on IR.
l9_contract_summary.clock_domain_protocol: m_can_hclk ≥ m_can_cclk; Sync block handles cross-domain handoff.
